scope: Diagnostic allocation interception on eight matched ABBA process runs, 128 persistent authenticated Chrome connections per run, two exact 1-MiB GETs and one exact 1-MiB PUT per connection. Allocation totals include startup, connection lifecycle and cleanup. No claim of zero steady-state allocations or acceptance of instrumented latency/residency.
method: Launch each client under heaptrack LD_PRELOAD, verify actual child executable/PID ownership, retain full traces; controlled client termination precedes interpreter flushing. Do not attach to running processes.
preflight: Exact candidate --help exited successfully under profiler; 245 allocation events observed. Preflight is separate from workload counts.
decision: Retain every paired total and peak, check payload integrity and FD recovery. Investigate any >5% increase in allocation counts; this short instrumented diagnostic is not a CPU/throughput performance verdict or a leak verdict.
bound: 900-second outer deadline, TERM invokes owned-process cleanup; 150-second final cleanup grace before forced termination. No other project process targeted.
correction: Attempt1 expected wrapper exit 0 after deliberately sending SIGTERM. Installed heaptrack script waits for its interpreter and propagates the debuggee exit status. Require a live client before teardown, full FD recovery, requested SIGTERM and wrapper exit 0 or 143; other exits fail. Parse every complete trace separately. Original failed attempt retained, not pooled.
